prompt: Make the jump feel forgiving: add 0.1 s of coyote time and variable jump height.

config.plan_model: Agent-tool model parameter 'sonnet' (Claude Code sub-agent; the harness did not report the resolved model id)
config.how: one fresh general-purpose sub-agent per plan, reads a job file with project brief + the developer prompt, writes numbered plan (<=8 steps, no code) via Write; not Claude Code plan mode

plans.text:
1. Read player.gd to learn how movement, gravity, jump input, and the floor check currently work, and check the Input Map for the jump action name.
2. Add exported tuning values for coyote duration (0.1 s), jump-cut multiplier, and optionally a short jump-buffer window so they can be tweaked in the Inspector without editing logic.
3. Track a coyote timer: reset it to full while the player is on the floor, and count it down each physics frame once they leave the ground.
4. Allow the jump when on the floor or while the coyote timer is still above zero, and clear the timer on jump so a second mid-air jump cannot happen.
5. Make sure walking off a ledge starts the countdown, but jumping upward does not, so coyote time never grants a double jump.
6. Implement variable jump height by cutting upward velocity (or applying stronger gravity) when the jump button is released while the player is still rising.
7. Keep the full-hold jump height the same as today, so only early release shortens the jump, and confirm the cut does not affect falling.
8. Playtest in level_01.tscn by running off platform edges, tapping versus holding jump, and testing against both enemy types and tile edges, then tune the values.

1. Read player.gd to understand how movement, gravity, jump input, and is_on_floor checks are currently structured, and note which input action and jump constants are already defined.
2. Add exported tuning variables for coyote time (0.1 s), jump velocity, and a jump-cut multiplier so the feel can be adjusted in the editor without touching logic.
3. Add a coyote timer that resets to full whenever the player is on the floor and counts down while airborne, so a jump is still allowed during the grace window after walking off a ledge.
4. Change the jump condition to check the coyote timer instead of strictly being on the floor, and zero the timer when a jump starts so the player cannot double-jump off the same ledge.
5. Implement variable jump height by cutting upward velocity when the jump button is released while the player is still rising, so a short tap gives a low hop and a hold gives the full jump.
6. Make sure the interaction is correct with existing behavior: enemy stomp bounces, knockback, and any other code that sets vertical velocity should not be accidentally cut or blocked by the new logic.
7. Playtest in level_01.tscn, checking ledge jumps just after leaving a platform, tap versus hold jumps, and jumping onto the TileMapLayer platforms, then tune the values.
8. Confirm no regressions in the rest of the scene (collisions, enemy interactions) and summarize the changes and tunable values for the developer.

1. Read player.gd to understand how movement, gravity, jump input, and is_on_floor() are currently handled, and check the Input Map for the existing jump action.
2. Add exported tuning variables on the Player for coyote time (default 0.1 s), jump release cut-off strength, and optionally a minimum jump hold, so values can be tweaked in the inspector without touching logic.
3. Implement a coyote timer: reset it to 0.1 s whenever the player is on the floor, count it down each physics frame while airborne, and treat the player as "able to jump" while the timer is above zero.
4. Change the jump trigger to use the "able to jump" condition instead of a strict floor check, and clear the coyote timer immediately when a jump starts so the player cannot double-jump from it.
5. Implement variable jump height: when the jump button is released while the player is still moving upward, cut the upward velocity (e.g. scale it down) so a short tap gives a low hop and a full hold gives the full jump.
6. Make sure the interactions are safe: coyote time should not trigger after jumping, after being launched by enemies or bounce pads, or when walking off a platform edge into a ledge-grab-like state, and the velocity cut must not affect falling or non-jump upward motion.
7. Playtest in level_01.tscn by walking off ledges at different moments and by tapping versus holding jump, then tune the exported values until the feel is forgiving without being floaty.
8. Check that the two enemy scenes and any stomp or bounce behavior still work with the changed jump logic, and note the new tuning variables for the developer.

1. Read player.gd to learn how movement, gravity, jump input, and is_on_floor() are currently handled, and check the Input Map for the jump action name.
2. Define tunable exported variables for coyote time (0.1 s) and for the variable-jump tuning (for example a jump-cut multiplier), so they can be adjusted in the Inspector without editing logic.
3. Add a coyote timer that resets to full while the player is on the floor and counts down once they leave a ledge, and make sure it is cleared when a jump is performed so it cannot grant a double jump.
4. Change the jump condition so a jump is allowed whenever the player is on the floor or the coyote timer is still above zero, keeping walking off a ledge distinct from jumping.
5. Implement variable jump height by cutting upward velocity when the jump button is released while the player is still rising, so a tap gives a short hop and a hold gives the full jump.
6. Verify the edge cases: no extra jump after landing, no effect from the cut when falling, and correct behavior on moving platforms or slopes in the TileMapLayer.
7. Playtest in level_01.tscn, jumping off ledges at the edge of the timing window and tapping versus holding the button, then tune the values until it feels forgiving but not floaty.
8. Check that the two enemy scenes and any bounce or stomp mechanics that set the player's velocity still work, and adjust them if they conflict with the jump-cut logic.

1. Read player.gd and the Project Settings input map to learn how movement, gravity, jump, and floor detection are currently handled, and note the existing jump input action name.
2. Define tunable values for coyote time (0.1 s) and jump-cut strength as exported variables on the Player so they can be adjusted in the editor without touching logic.
3. Add coyote time tracking: while the player is on the floor, keep a timer refilled to 0.1 s; when they leave the floor, count it down so a jump is still allowed during that window.
4. Change the jump condition so a press is valid if the player is on the floor or the coyote timer is still above zero, and consume the timer on jumping so no double jump is possible.
5. Make sure walking off a ledge and jumping into the air (a normal fall) does not grant coyote time after an actual jump, by zeroing the timer at jump start.
6. Add variable jump height: when the jump button is released while the player is still moving upward, reduce the upward velocity (cut it) so a short tap yields a lower jump than a held press.
7. Verify interactions with the rest of the game, such as enemy stomp bounces or other code that sets vertical velocity, so the jump-cut only applies to player-initiated jumps.
8. Playtest in level_01.tscn on ledges and platforms, tune the values for feel, and confirm no regressions such as double jumps or jump-cut firing on falling.
